cards.explanation: The answer is that the law of the Spirit of life set them free from the law of sin and death. Romans 8:2 says it plainly: “…the law of the Spirit of life set you free from the law of sin and death.” Free means free, friends. That's an unlocked door, not a bigger ring of keys.

The answer is that God sent His own Son as an offering for sin. Romans 8:3 says God did it “…by sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful man, as an offering for sin.” The law couldn't do it, so God did it by sending His Son. I'm just standing here with my mustache in the air.

The answer is True. Romans 8:3 says God sent His Son “…as an offering for sin. He thus condemned sin in the flesh…” Look where the condemning lands, friends: on sin. Verse 1 already told us there's no condemnation for those in Christ Jesus.

The answer is so the law's righteous standard is fulfilled in us. Romans 8:4 says it was “…so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us…” Fulfilled, not thrown out. God had a purpose, and it was good.

The answer is life. Romans 8:6 says, “The mind of the flesh is death, but the mind of the Spirit is life and peace…” Life AND peace, friends. Read that one twice, because it sounds even better the second time.

The answer is because it is hostile to God. Romans 8:7 gives the reason: “…because the mind of the flesh is hostile to God…” It goes on to say that it “…does not submit to God’s law, nor can it do so.” Hostile is a strong word, and the verse chose it.

The answer is False. Romans 8:8 says, “Those controlled by the flesh cannot please God.” The word is cannot, friends, and it's one the verse doesn't soften. And right after it comes the good news for those with the Spirit (Romans 8:9).
The answer is belong. Romans 8:9 says, “And if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Christ.” Belong is the word, friends. It's about whose you are, not just what you do.

The answer is True, and it's a big one. Romans 8:11 says, “…He who raised Christ Jesus from the dead will also give life to your mortal bodies through His Spirit, who lives in you.” Notice the "if" at the start, bakers: if the Spirit of the One who raised Jesus lives in you. I'd shout, but my mustache is already waving.
The answer is live. Romans 8:13 says, “…if by the Spirit you put to death the deeds of the body, you will live.” Die on one side, live on the other. The verse doesn't leave much room in the middle.

The answer is the Spirit of adoption to sonship. Romans 8:15 says, “…you received the Spirit of adoption to sonship, by whom we cry, 'Abba! Father!'” Not a spirit of slavery that returns you to fear, but the Spirit of adoption, friends. The verse puts the two side by side.

The answer is the Spirit Himself. Romans 8:16 says, “The Spirit Himself testifies with our spirit that we are God’s children.” The Spirit speaks with our spirit. I'd say that's about as good a witness as you can ask for.

The answer is heirs of God. Romans 8:17 says, “And if we are children, then we are heirs: heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ…” Children means heirs, friends. The verse goes right from one to the other.

The answer is suffer with Him. Romans 8:17 says, “…if indeed we suffer with Him, so that we may also be glorified with Him.” It's a heavy word, friends, and I'll say that plainly. The verse puts suffering with Him and being glorified with Him together.
